title: Dedicated capacity weekly prep - Hannah Kim
content:
Weekly prep notes for Dedicated Capacity sync (1:1 + team follow-up)

Context / goal:
- Prep for weekly sync with Jordan (eng manager) and Alex (product) to align on GPU pool forecasts, reservations to propose for next quarter, and autoscaling tuning.
- Outcome: agree on target reservation commits for Q2, list of urgent scaling actions, and owners for follow-ups.

Quick summary / TL;DR:
- Current committed pool: 120 A100-eq GPUs (mixture of A100 40GB and 80GB).
- Baseline utilization (last 30 days): 72% avg; peak 95% during eval windows.
- Forecast ask from sales/CS for next quarter: +36 GPUs starting mid-April for 4 large customers (staged across regions).
- Recommendation: increase committed reserve by 30% (-> ~156 GPUs) with optional burst capacity enabled; keep autoscaling headroom at 25% for latency SLOs.
- Risks: budget approval timing (sales renewal windows), procurement lead time for dedicated hardware in EMEA, potential impact to unit cost if we oversize.

Agenda (30 min):
1) 0-5m quick status: utilization, incidents, runway (me)
2) 5-15m forecast review: customer asks & projection (Alex)
3) 15-22m reservation proposal: commit size, phasing, regional split (me)
4) 22-27m autoscaling policy update: thresholds, burst config, cooldowns (Jordan)
5) 27-30m actions & owners + next steps (all)

Data / numbers to reference:
- Current pool: 120 GPUs (80GB x60, 40GB x60) across us-west-2 (60), eu-west-1 (40), ap-northeast-1 (20).
- Avg tokens/hour served (hosted + dedicated routes): 1.8B tokens/day; dedicated accounts ~22% of tokens but account for ~38% of GPU-hours due to long-context workloads.
- Last 30-day utilization breakdown: 72% avg, 95% 95th percentile. Nightly maintenance windows cause 6% drop for 02:00-04:00 UTC.
- Queueing incidents: 3 incidents last month where queue growth > 60s; root cause: concurrent eval jobs + low burst cap in eu-west-1.

Forecast assumptions (for proposal):
- Sales commitments: 4 customers requesting combined 36 GPUs (April-June). Staged: 12 GPUs mid-April, +12 in May, +12 in June.
- Organic growth baseline: +8% GPU-hours QoQ.
- Safety buffer: 20% to cover eval campaigns and internal perf tests.
- Procurement lead: prefer cloud reservations but consider Dedicated hardware procurement times (6-8 weeks).

Proposal (recommended):
- Commit to +36 GPUs (net) for Q2 but provision as follows:
  - Phase 1 (Apr 15): +12 GPUs in us-west-2 (closest to largest customer).
  - Phase 2 (May 15): +12 GPUs in eu-west-1 (to cover EU customer and burst).
  - Phase 3 (Jun 1): +12 GPUs ap-northeast-1 (give APAC visibility).
- Keep 20% of newly committed capacity as flexible (reassignable across regions) for first 60 days.
- Maintain burst pool of 24 GPUs (spot/ephemeral) to absorb unexpected peaks; configure preemptible fallback for non-critical batch evals.
- Autoscaling config: target utilization 65% (scale-out at >=72% over 3m window), scale-in threshold <=45% with cooldown 10m, max scale step 16 GPUs.

Cost / economics note:
- If we commit +36 GPUs, expected committed cost increase ~ $70k/month (estimate; need finance confirmation).
- Unit cost per token likely improves due to better KV cache hit rate as more long-context work consolidates on dedicated pools; estimate 5-8% token cost improvement for dedicated customers.

Open questions / things to resolve before committing:
- Finance sign-off timeline for +$70k/month (Priya to confirm).
- SLA implications for regional partial commitments (if we move GPUs between regions).
- Can release-engineering shorten deployment testing to 3 weeks instead of 6 for new hardware? (ask release-eng).
- Confirm whether any existing long-running eval campaigns can be rescheduled to reduce April peak.

Talking points for Jordan (1:1):
- How aggressive do we want to be on reservations vs. relying on burst capacity? (tradeoff: lower latency vs. higher monthly commit)
- Are we comfortable with 20% flexible pool during Q2 ramp, or should we aim for 10% to reduce cost?
- Do we have headcount to manage cross-region placement and rebalancing (ops effort)?

Action items (owners + dates):
- Priya (Finance): confirm budget availability and required approval path for $70k/month delta. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Alex (Product): validate customer start dates and whether any can be pushed to May to smooth ramp. Due: 2026-03-03.
- Jordan (Eng Manager): agree on autoscaling thresholds and sign off on scale step limits. Due: 2026-03-04 (end of sync).
- Release Eng (assigned: Miguel Torres): estimate deployment testing time for new hardware and whether we can compress to 3 weeks. Due: 2026-03-06.
- Me (Hannah): prepare committed-reservation proposal document for finance (with cost breakdown) and circulate. Due: 2026-03-05.

Follow-ups for next weekly sync:
- Present final cost/commitment proposal for decision.
- Rollout plan for phased capacity increases with timelines and test validations.
- Post-mortem on last queueing incidents and mitigation steps taken.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider offering customers short-term discounted burst packages (30-day) to defer long-term commitment while keeping revenue.
- Track KV cache hit improvements after consolidation; run a targeted benchmark 2 weeks after phase 2.
- If finance pushback, propose a hybrid: commit +18 GPUs and rely on cloud burst for remaining demand; recalc cost tradeoff.

Attachments to build before sync:
- spreadsheet: short-term capacity plan + cost model (sheet id -> attach to confluence)
- perf: 95th percentile latency graphs by region for last 14 days
- incidents: short write-up of last 3 queueing incidents (root causes)

-- end of notes --
